image_description: A close-up, high-resolution photograph of a green tiger beetle (Cicindelinae) resting on a textured wooden surface. The beetle exhibits vibrant metallic green coloration with distinct white/cream markings on its elytra. Its head is broad with large compound eyes and visible mandibles. Six slender legs are visible, gripping the wood grain. Antennae are present but partially blend with the background.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head broader than pronotum with large prominent compound eyes.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is clearly visible, appearing wider than the thorax segment behind it. The large, bulging compound eyes are a dominant feature and match the description perfectly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Long sickle-shaped mandibles adapted for capturing prey.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mandibles are visible protruding from the front of the head. They appear elongated and curved, consistent with the 'sickle-shaped' description for this species.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Filiform antennae extending well beyond the midbody.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While antennae bases are visible, the full length cannot be confirmed to extend 'well beyond the midbody' due to perspective and blending with the background texture. One antenna is visible but seems shorter than the body length in this projection.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated, slender body with distinctly narrow proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is oval but elongated, typical of carabid beetles. The proportions look natural and slender relative to the head size.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bright metallic coloration in green, bronze, or copper tones.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The exoskeleton displays a vivid, iridescent metallic green sheen, matching the 'green' tone specification exactly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Distinctive pale markings on smooth iridescent elytra.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There are clear, irregular cream-colored spots on the rear half of the elytra, which is a key diagnostic feature for many tiger beetle species.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Six slender cursorial legs enabling rapid pursuit.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: All six legs are visible. They are long, thin, and jointed, consistent with cursorial (running) adaptations. No extra or missing limbs are detected.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Chitinous exoskeleton with segmented body (head, thorax, abdomen).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The segmentation between head, pronotum (thorax), and elytra (covering abdomen) is distinct. The texture appears hard and chitinous.

The very end of the right hind leg (tarsus/claws) appears to merge slightly with the wood crack rather than sitting distinctly on top of it. The geometry is ambiguous at the contact point.
